subject.title: fix(whatsapp): suppress typing for unmentioned group runs regardless of delivery mode

question: Should OpenClaw accept suppressing WhatsApp typing for all unmentioned non-command group runs, including automatic-delivery runs that might later send a proactive visible reply?
rationale: Current main preserves typing for automatic WhatsApp group replies, while this PR changes that user-visible feedback boundary to avoid false typing on silent background runs; tests can prove mechanics but not the preferred UX tradeoff.

options.title: Approve A Rebased Narrow Mitigation
options.body: Refresh this branch onto the current `conversationKind` and group-mention path, keep command and mention carve-outs, and accept that proactive visible unmentioned replies may arrive without a typing indicator.

options.title: Prefer Visible-Delivery Typing
options.body: Use the broader send-start boundary from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/90477 after its conflict and compatibility review are resolved.

options.title: Keep Current Automatic Typing
options.body: Reject this broader suppression and keep typing indicators for automatic unmentioned group replies until a structural delivery-boundary fix is ready.

recommendation.title: Approve A Rebased Narrow Mitigation
recommendation.body: Refresh this branch onto the current `conversationKind` and group-mention path, keep command and mention carve-outs, and accept that proactive visible unmentioned replies may arrive without a typing indicator.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main ownership of the affected WhatsApp dispatch shape and typing lifecycle makes this the best available routing candidate for the UX boundary choice.
